item: Rows 379 (R808) and 385: a restore places only the key files this app creates, by the exact names an erase uses; evidence_ml_dsa_65.key leaves that list
summary: An erase treats the data folder's keys as the app's only while it holds nothing but src.safety.data_scope.APP_KEY_NAMES (R806/R807), but a restore placed any file the backup's keys folder carried ('carried as it is', carried_unread), and _key_slot took any '<who>_ed25519.pem', so one backup could leave the folder holding names the app never makes and turn the next erase's verdict into 'folder kept'. merge._APP_KEY_FILES is now derived from APP_KEY_NAMES (less the restored-key marker, R801), so restore and erase read ONE list; every other member of the keys role is not written, stays in the backup and is listed with the reason 'not a key this app creates; it is not written and stays in the backup' (x12); every member refused by its name (that, a restored-key marker spelling, or an unsafe spelling, now including a path written another way such as keys/./x, per the two security reads) is counted in not_app_keys {count, listed}, and only the first 50 are listed in not_placed, under a name made printable (console_safe) and cut to 120 characters; the import report adds a line for the ones beyond the cap. The restore still completes. carried_unread is gone (always empty now). Residual, stated in the release note (Plan's wording): where an earlier restore already placed another key file there, an erase in a folder the app did not choose keeps that file and counts it among the items the app did not create; in a folder the app chose it is destroyed as before. 8 new tests fail on the old code; two R801/R448 tests that pinned the carrying were rewritten to the ruling. Row 385 (Plan, under R807/R808): evidence_ml_dsa_65.key is out of APP_KEY_NAMES, since no version of the app ever wrote it (git log -S over every ref; only custody and annotations make ML-DSA keys), so neither an erase nor a restore treats it as the app's; lane D confirmed nothing on its side pins the old seven-name set.
